findings.title: Memory-bounding regression in base64 alignment loop (partial CVE-2026-108147 regression)
findings.description: The previous fix for CVE-2026-108147 guaranteed that at most one chunk (plus a 3-byte remainder) was held in memory before decoded data was handed to upload handlers. The new alignment loop calls `field_stream.read(self._chunk_size)` repeatedly until the accumulated stripped length is a multiple of 4. In an adversarial payload where base64 characters are sparsely distributed among whitespace (e.g., one base64 char per 64 KB of newlines), the loop can consume many full chunks before alignment is reached, buffering all stripped bytes in `stripped_parts` before a single `b64decode` call. The total is still bounded by the upload size, but the peak in-memory footprint before the first `handler.receive_data_chunk()` call can exceed `FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE` by up to the accumulated alignment data. This partially regresses the memory-bounding guarantee that the CVE fix established.
findings.suggestion: Cap the number of alignment iterations (e.g., `max_align_reads = 4`) or fall back to the old remainder-carry approach when the alignment loop exceeds one extra chunk. Alternatively, decode and flush the already-aligned prefix before reading the next alignment chunk, so that data is handed to handlers incrementally: ```python while stripped_length % 4 != 0: over_chunk = field_stream.read(self._chunk_size) if not over_chunk: break over_stripped = b"".join(over_chunk.split()) stripped_parts.append(over_stripped) stripped_length += len(over_stripped) # If we've accumulated more than 2 chunks, flush the aligned prefix if len(stripped_parts) > 2: aligned = stripped_length // 4 * 4 prefix = b"".join(stripped_parts)[:aligned] chunk = base64.b64decode(prefix, validate=True) # ... pass to handler, reset stripped_parts ... ``` ---

findings.title: Silent acceptance of truncated base64 uploads (removed input-validation error)
